## Verified

I reviewed the expense claims interface against the engineering policy and production readiness:

**Critical findings:**
- **Non-functional UI**: HTML has no input fields despite telling users to "enter an amount and pick a category"
- **No input binding**: Frontend app.js doesn't bind user inputs to the submission state—users can't actually enter data
- **Missing category validation**: Server accepts any category without defining valid options
- **No authentication**: API lacks user identification and authorization checks
- **Inadequate tests**: Only one trivial test; missing happy-path and error-case coverage
- **Policy violations**: Fails to clarify unknowns, validate at boundaries, and test before claiming completion

The interface cannot be released. A user couldn't submit a claim even if they tried—the form lacks all interactive elements. Release verdict written to REVIEW.md.
